extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO discipline, OED staff, and members of the public interested in USPTO disciplinary actions
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions governing discipline of practitioners before the USPTO (reciprocal discipline, suspension terms, limited recognition to wind up matters, publication and notice obligations, and reinstatement requirements) as set out in a Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Director may impose reciprocal discipline based on a state disciplinary order; a "Notice and Order Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24" informs the respondent and initiates the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent seeks to contest imposition of suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response "containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the [state court] would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)." Failure to file a response may lead the USPTO Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's suspension by a state court can constitute a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), providing ground for USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, the USPTO suspension was "for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being suspended by the Supreme Court of California." The state suspension itself was predicated on violations of California Rules of Professional Conduct (discussed below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct: non-lawyer management and fee-sharing (state predicate violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was found to have violated professional conduct rules by: (1) employing a non-lawyer to act as office manager for a satellite office; (2) paying the non-lawyer a percentage of net profits generated by the satellite office; (3) permitting the non-lawyer to conduct client intakes and oversee processing and settlement of cases without Respondent's supervision; and (4) forming a partnership with a non-lawyer where the partnership's activities consisted of the practice of law, aiding a non-lawyer in the unauthorized practice of law, and sharing legal fees with a non-lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These predicate facts supported violations of California Rules of Professional Conduct 1-310, 1-300(A), and 1-320(A). The Notice summarizes these specific misconduct examples as illustrative of the types of conduct that can give rise to reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and structure of sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order suspended Respondent from practice before the Office for one year, "with all but the first 60 days of the suspension stayed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order also granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order, to allow winding up of client matters. The structure (length, stay, limited recognition period) exemplifies how the USPTO may tailor sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition and wind-up/withdrawal obligations (37 C.F.R. § 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of this Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of this Final Order." During limited recognition the respondent is directed "to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly directs the practitioner not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition. This demonstrates the USPTO practice of limited recognition solely to permit orderly termination of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order directs that during the 30 days of limited recognition the respondent is "directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational constraint during the wind-up period and is tied to the limited recognition timeframe; violating it would be inconsistent with the purpose of limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette detailing the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice as printed in the order contains: respondent's name and registration number, the fact and duration of suspension, the specific regulation violated (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)), the predicate state rules violated (California Rules of Professional Conduct numbers), and a summary of the factual bases for the state suspension (non-lawyer management, fee sharing, unauthorized practice, etc.). Disciplinary decisions are also posted to the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision ensures reciprocal communication of disciplinary actions and the grounds for them to relevant jurisdictions and forums where the practitioner is admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order directs that "Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 governs practice limitations and notification requirements during suspension (e.g., prohibition on practice before the Office, notification duties), so compliance is required as a condition of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order directs that "Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.60 prescribes the process and requirements for seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO after discipline; compliance with its provisions is mandatory when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites federal statutory authority (35 U.S.C.) and USPTO regulations as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline and for publication/notice obligations.
